1.rationale: The lede states the complete finding with all key numbers (Sept 9 to Oct 7, 28 days, 606 to 692 mm, 43 to 72 mm) before any chart, and each plate carries a bold prose caption stating its finding in words. A reader who never decodes a chart gets the full story from the lede, the plate captions, the inter-plate prose, and the full-record table.

2.rationale: Every plate is named and captioned by its actual finding; gaps are drawn as open dashed bands, era means as short rules only where the annotations name them, and Plate III is explicitly drawn from zero. Plate II's non-zero baseline is a position encoding self-disclosed in the caption ('starts at 550 mm, not zero, to show the drift'), which keeps it honest.

3.rationale: All four traps surface in every relevant view: the seam, gaps, hollow 2019, and era rules recur as keyed annotations (a-d) on all three plates, in the lede caveat, as labeled NO RECORD rows and an UNVERIFIED note in the table, and again in About; era averages are built from verified years only. The 'not its cause' scope claim appears in the lede and About with zero attribution language anywhere.

4.rationale: 'The weir has kept the valley's time for a generation' and 'it is the lane under water in October, and the parish answering in its own practical way' are patient, place-loving local-paper prose. Both human-context fragments sit exactly where they serve the data (the meadow quote after the onset plate, the sandbag minutes after the totals plate), not as decoration.

5.rationale: Classical broadsheet typography — serif display, italic standfirst, comfortable measure, clear plate/annotation/table hierarchy — carries a genuinely long read in both modes, and the mobile renders keep charts and annotations legible with clean wrapping. The dotted-rule table is disciplined even at 34 rows.

6.rationale: There is no scrollytelling at all: the entire page is a fully readable static base with natural scroll, so nothing paces the reader and reduced-motion parity is complete by construction. Machine gates confirm both modes render faithfully.

7.rationale: 'The reporter's notes written on the record itself' is a clean one-sentence idea that every layer executes — the standfirst declares it, all three plates do it, About echoes it. It is superbly executed annotated charting, but the form remains three conventional plates walked by prose rather than a shape that itself embodies the season's movement.

8.rationale: Both declared breaks (journalism inked onto the plates; grid suppressed except where the story points) are visibly executed exactly as declared, and reading mechanics stay fully conventional. I found no undeclared convention break; the Plate II baseline is disclosed in-caption rather than smuggled.

9.rationale: The prose is unsensational and specific to this valley — weir, fair, lane, parish — and lines like 'not a dramatic year here or there but a patient drift' could not be lifted into another paper unchanged. Register holds steady from lede to About.

10.rationale: There are no effects detached from reporting anywhere; every device on the page — annotation keys, gap bands, era rules, the hollow 2019 mark — is itself a piece of the reporting and traces directly to a fact in the sealed record. This is the criterion's inversion achieved in full.

1.rationale: The bold lede delivers the whole finding with numbers before the rail begins, a 'what it shows' paragraph states the rail's conclusion in plain text, and mid-rail asides narrate the pattern in words. A reader who never engages the rail still gets the full story from lede, description, asides, and About.

2.rationale: The rail is named and described by its actual finding, gaps are hatched NO RECORD rows, and the fixed 550-750 mm bar scale is declared with true values printed on every line. Still, bar length from a non-zero baseline visually exaggerates the 14% rise, a mild encoding blemish that disclosure mitigates but does not remove.

3.rationale: The 1997 seam is a full-width structural heading inside the record, the three missing years are hatched labeled rows with reasons, 2019 gets a hollow dot with an inline red UNVERIFIED note (preserved on mobile), and About restates all of it including exclusion from averages. Scope is held: 'the page describes the shift, not its cause.'

4.rationale: The interjections are the craft: 'the dots edging rightward, the bars a shade longer each wet year than the valley had been used to' is patient local journalism placed at data-motivated points. The 1994 weir-keeper quote sits chronologically inside the rail where it belongs, and the 2022 flood minutes close the record.

5.rationale: Serif headline, italic deck, letterspaced era headings, and clean row rhythm carry the long rail well in both modes, and the mobile restructuring into stacked year blocks stays legible without overflow. The 34-row rail grows slightly monotonous on mobile and leans on a dense how-to-read block, which keeps it just below the top typographic tier.

6.rationale: The 'watch the season walk down the page' reading is native scroll on a fully readable static base — no scrollytelling, no hijack, no pacing imposed on the reader. Reduced-motion parity is complete by construction.

7.rationale: 'The record itself is the reading matter' is the strongest felt-form idea of the three: reading down 34 ruled lines the reader physically watches the onset dot walk later and the bars grow heavier, which IS the finding. Title deck, how-to-read, interjections, and About all reinforce the one sentence.

8.rationale: Both declared breaks (rail as the only chart; editorial interjections inside the record) are executed exactly as declared and the reading mechanics stay conventional scroll-and-read. I found no undeclared break; the bar scale is declared in the how-to-read block rather than hidden.

9.rationale: 'Like the almanac the valley used to keep' and 'longer each wet year than the valley had been used to' are specific, unsensational, and unmistakably this valley's paper. The voice holds through the asides and About without a single dramatized phrase.

10.rationale: The signature device is the dataset's own form — a yearly ledger — and every interruption of it traces to something the record actually contains (decade turns, the seam, the gaps, 2019). Nothing on the page is effect detached from reporting.

1.rationale: The finding leads twice in plain text: the bold lede with all numbers, then the then/now diptych giving the conclusion as labeled figures with 'the difference, ink to ink: 28 days later, 86 mm more a season, 29 mm more on the worst day.' A no-scroll, no-chart reader gets the complete story before the first plot.

2.rationale: The single drift chart is named and described by its actual finding, uses a natural Sep 1-Oct 15 domain, draws the three missing years as open shaded bands, the seam as a dashed rule, and 2019 hollow. The totals and worst-day series are carried honestly by disclosed era figures and the full table rather than charts, with nothing distorted.

3.rationale: Promoting the method change to the page's ink system means the central caveat travels with literally every figure, era label, and table row, always with era names written out; gaps and the 2019 UNVERIFIED flag appear in chart, table, and About; the diptych explicitly excludes 2019 and averages only verified years. Scope discipline is explicit: 'the page describes the shift, not its cause.'

4.rationale: 'The record keeps human time as well as rain' and the quotes labeled 'a gauge year' / 'a weir year' bind the human fragments into the ink system rather than using them as decoration. But connective narrative prose is sparser than the other candidates — the middle of the page reads more as structured statistics than a walked story.

5.rationale: The diptych's letterspaced kickers and two-ink serif figures are handsome editorial typography, and both modes and both viewports hold up with the mobile diptych stacking cleanly. The full-record table occupies a large share of the page, tilting the lower half toward ledger rather than long-read rhythm.

6.rationale: A static, fully readable page with no scrollytelling, no scrolljack, and nothing pacing the reader; reduced-motion parity is complete by construction. Both mode renders are faithful.

7.rationale: 'Two inks for two instruments — read the story by watching the blue drift from the umber' is one sentence that genuinely governs every layer: masthead legend, colored era words in the lede, diptych, chart, quotes, and table ink. The answer-first diptych plus the ink seam makes the then/now shift felt, though the 'lands harder' half is felt only through figures, not form.

8.rationale: Both declared breaks (instrument-colored ink system, never color alone; finding-first diptych before the time series) are executed precisely as declared, with era names written out at every crossing I checked. Reading mechanics stay conventional and I found no undeclared break.

9.rationale: 'The town weir's ledger, printed in two inks' and the gauge-year/weir-year labels are specific and unsensational, but the voice lives mostly in labels and apparatus; sustained prose passages that only this paper could run are fewer than in the strongest candidate.

10.rationale: The page's one flourish is the dataset's own integrity caveat promoted to form — the exact opposite of effect detached from reporting — and every other device (gap bands, hollow 2019, era rules, quotes-by-ink) traces to a fact in the sealed record. Nothing here is imitation spectacle.
